leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer optical lattice clocks as a two-laureate prize for Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye, with near-identical citations (invention and realisation or development of the clock at the 10^-18 level). They share the view that credit is clean (magic-wavelength concept plus record performance) and that the result is reproduced. They differ in how much weight to give the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes as overlap, in how far other lattice-clock groups (SYRTE, PTB, NIST/JILA, RIKEN) are left uncredited, and in the pending redefinition of the second (a reason to wait, or already a reason to act). All four list B017 and B016 as alternatives, with B017 named first by each. Several supporters state that opening-round agreement is not itself evidence of merit.

Three members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, with citations that combine the flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. They share the view that it is a rare prediction-plus-experiment discovery that opened a new field and has been reproduced by many groups, and that the citation should avoid claiming an explanation of the superconductivity. They differ on how mature a 2018 discovery with an unresolved pairing mechanism is: Danielsson-Ulf and Mehlig-Bernhard treat the mechanism as irrelevant to a discovery prize, while Johansson-Goran is less relaxed about maturity. Johansson-Goran lists B012 and B015 as alternatives, Danielsson-Ulf lists B015 and B051, and Mehlig-Bernhard lists B015 and B003. Among other members, Eriksson-Olle would credit only two names, and Pearce-Mark and Kroll-Stefan raise credit-boundary and maturity concerns without ruling it out.

One member prefers time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, on the grounds of a complete theory-plus-experiment chain, two decades of confirmation and a conceptual change in band-structure classification. Eriksson-Olle acknowledges this is a minority position, with B017 and B015 as alternatives. Danielsson-Ulf lists B051 as an alternative but would credit Hasan rather than Mele. Several members cite unresolved credit (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang; 2D versus 3D work) and the 2016 topological-phases prize as obstacles.

areas_of_agreement: B015, B017 and B051 are all described as secure, reproduced discoveries or inventions; no member disputes that the underlying results are real.

Every member whose preferred configuration differs from B015 or B017 names one of them as an alternative: Eriksson-Olle lists B017 and B015; Johansson-Goran, Danielsson-Ulf and Mehlig-Bernhard each list B015 as an alternative to B017; Kroll-Stefan, Lindroth-Eva, Olsson-Eva and Pearce-Mark each list B017 first among their alternatives.

Johansson-Goran, who works on circuit QED, discounts own first opening choice B012 partly because of the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits; Olsson-Eva, Kroll-Stefan, Mehlig-Bernhard and Pearce-Mark also say that a second prize in that family so soon needs a distinct justification. No file prefers B012.
Members on both sides accept that any B017 citation should name the prediction and the observation of the phases, not the pairing mechanism or the wider twistronics field.
Members on both sides accept that the opening-round count is not itself evidence of merit, and that field proximity should be disclosed.
scientific_disputes: Whether a precision-measurement invention (B015) should rank above a discovery that opened a new regime of physics (B017); B015 supporters stress an unambiguous figure of merit and concrete downstream uses, while B017 supporters and several B015 supporters acknowledge B017 as broader in reach.

Whether the lattice clock is a distinct step from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes (magic-wavelength many-atom parallelism, per Kroll-Stefan, Olsson-Eva and Pearce-Mark) or an incremental advance in a recognised line (per Danielsson-Ulf and the case-against statements).
Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and the 2010 prize on graphene make B051 and B017 harder to justify, or whether the Z2 insulator and moire matter are distinct discoveries.

Whether the downstream payoff of the lattice clock (redefinition of the second, geodesy, dark-matter searches) is still prospective, as Eriksson-Olle and Johansson-Goran argue, or already concrete, as B015 supporters argue.

Whether biomolecular condensates (B003), which only Mehlig-Bernhard names as an alternative, count as physics in the relevant sense; Lindroth-Eva reads it mainly as cell biology and Kroll-Stefan is unsure whether all condensates are genuine phases.
attribution_disputes: B015: both Katori and Ye are proposed by every supporter, but Lindroth-Eva and Pearce-Mark raise whether other lattice-clock groups (SYRTE, PTB, NIST, JILA colleagues of Ye) and ion-clock or comb figures are left out; Lindroth-Eva also asks whether adding a third name would blur the invention.

B017: all three B017 supporters list MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, but Eriksson-Olle would credit only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and Mehlig-Bernhard would accept two names if a compact citation is preferred; members dispute whether Bistritzer is a necessary joint author of the 2011 prediction or a padding of the theory side.

B017: members note that Yuan Cao, the Dean, Young, Kim and Yazdani groups and earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) fall outside the credited names; Olsson-Eva, Johansson-Goran and Mehlig-Bernhard describe the omission of Cao as a difficulty the citation cannot repair.

B051: Kane and Molenkamp are common to all proposals, but members disagree whether the third seat goes to Mele (Eriksson-Olle) or Hasan (Danielsson-Ulf), and whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal sits outside the credited names; members state that Zhang is deceased, which this summary does not verify.

B016 (alternative for Kroll-Stefan, Lindroth-Eva, Olsson-Eva and Pearce-Mark): five credited names for three places; the experimentalist trio and a theory-weighted trio are described as differing, and Pearce-Mark notes that an experimentalist trio would leave out Zoller, Cirac and Jaksch.
maturity_disputes: B017: the 2018 discovery and the unresolved superconducting mechanism. Danielsson-Ulf and Mehlig-Bernhard say the discovery is secure and reproduced and the mechanism is an interpretation question; Johansson-Goran, Olsson-Eva and Pearce-Mark treat it as a timing concern, with Eriksson-Olle saying a disputed mechanism should be reflected in the citation wording.
B015: whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the second, which Pearce-Mark and Kroll-Stefan state could be read either way.

Danielsson-Ulf argues that the maturity test applied to B017 should be applied consistently to pulsar-timing evidence for a gravitational-wave background (B004), which appears in Pearce-Mark's opening ranking; Johansson-Goran and Pearce-Mark express caution about the significance of the individual pulsar-timing arrays.
B051 is described as the most mature of the three leading candidates, with about two decades of confirmation, while the committee is said to have thinner support for it.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-Goran: works on circuit QED theory, is a colleague of Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson at Chalmers and directs WACQT; flags a possible recusal issue for B012 and therefore does not prefer it. No flagged conflict for B015, B017 or B051.
Olsson-Eva: shares an institution (Chalmers) with Johansson-Goran and would flag or recuse if Chalmers colleagues were named in B012; no conflict for B015.

Lindroth-Eva: documented collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond group; no documented tie to Katori or Ye, but flagged to the chair for the committee to decide whether B015 needs any recusal.

Kroll-Stefan: doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder (Hall is not a candidate) and shared laser-stabilisation techniques; involvement in WACQT and quantum-information work close to B016, B011, B010, B012 and B029, so views on those are to be discounted; no specific conflict for B015.

Eriksson-Olle and Mehlig-Bernhard: field adjacency noted (electronic-structure theory near B051 and B017; statistical physics near B003), with no personal or institutional tie to any credited name. Danielsson-Ulf and Pearce-Mark report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee treat the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes as a reason to reduce the weight of B015, and can B015 supporters state which element of the lattice clock is not covered by those prizes?
If the committee prefers a discovery that opened a new regime of physics over a measurement invention, does B017 then rank ahead of B015, and which members change their ordering under that criterion?

For B017, is the superconducting mechanism a reason to defer, or can a citation limited to the prediction of flat bands and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states resolve the maturity objection?

For B017, should the laureates be MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, or MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero only, and can the committee agree a defensible position on Yuan Cao and the other experimental groups?
For B015, can members who raised other lattice-clock groups or ion-clock figures state whether any named individual should replace or join Katori and Ye, or confirm the two-name configuration?
For B051, who holds the third seat (Mele or Hasan), and how does the committee weigh the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 2016 topological-phases prize?

Should the committee regard a prize for B012 or other superconducting-circuit work as ruled out by the 2025 award, and does any member wish to restore B012 or B016 to their preferred configuration with a three-person split?

Given the disclosed proximity of Lindroth-Eva to the Lund attosecond group, of Kroll-Stefan to the Boulder precision-spectroscopy lineage and of Johansson-Goran and Olsson-Eva at Chalmers, does the committee require any recusal before the final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: Round-1 preferred configurations split four for B015, three for B017 and one for B051, with no member preferring any other shortlisted candidate. B015 or B017 appears among the alternatives of every member, and B016 is an alternative for four members. The scientific reality of the leading candidates is not disputed; the open issues are distinctness from earlier prizes for B015, maturity and credit boundaries for B017, and the third laureate for B051. As chair, I prefer B015 myself and have tried to state the B017 and B051 positions on their own terms.
